short: Unit target (M02) and unit-conditioned vocoder (M06) are standard; units cut LRS3 WER 21.8 points, AV-HuBERT 20.4 more, the vocoder 0.3; unit gain untested on AV-HuBERT, single runs.
position: The paper [@choi2023intelligible] changes the training target (M02, 200 HuBERT units predicted beside the mel-spectrogram) and the vocoder (M06, conditioned on units and a speaker embedding); both are standard. The units carry the content gain (LRS3 ASR WER 72.5% to 50.7%, one run), the vocoder and mel augmentation move WER by 0.3 and 0.2 points (Table 3), and the headline 29.8% comes from swapping in a pretrained AV-HuBERT encoder, a step of 20.4 points (41% relative) against 21.8 points (30%) for the units, with the unit gain never measured on that encoder. The [concurrent] ReVISE also predicts HuBERT units from an AV-HuBERT-initialised encoder, at 33.9% [@hsu2023revise]; the [later] V2SFlow is 1.3 points lower with the same ASR model, and its listeners rate the target 2.46 of 5 for naturalness, while the paper's own 4.40 comes from its non-AV-HuBERT variant on 20 clips [@choi2024v2sflow]. The input includes a speaker embedding from a speech segment of unstated origin, and no result is repeated over seeds.
